questions.prompt: If another vehicle is following too close, what should a driver do?
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating, don't brake suddenly or speed up. Slow down gradually and give them a chance to pass. Key words: "to pass".

choices.text: Slow down gradually and encourage the other vehicle to pass
Press hard on the brake pedal
Increase speed to 10 km/h above the posted speed limit

questions.prompt: According to the law in Alberta, it is the driver's responsibility to ensure that all passengers under what age are properly restrained in the vehicle?
questions.explanation: The driver must make sure every passenger under 16 is wearing a seat belt or is in the correct child seat. Passengers 16 and older are responsible for themselves. Key words: "all passengers".

questions.prompt: In Alberta, the law requires that seat belts must be worn:
questions.explanation: Alberta law requires seat belts to be worn and properly adjusted at all times while the vehicle is moving.

choices.text: Only when driving at highway speeds
Only when driving in the city

questions.prompt: Using the 2-second rule to judge a safe following distance when driving:
questions.explanation: The 2-second rule measures time, not distance, so the gap grows automatically as you go faster and the rule works at any speed. Leave more time in poor road or weather conditions. Key words: "any speed".

choices.text: Is more accurate on rural highways than in urban centres
Is not accurate at speeds greater than 100 km/h
Is not accurate at speeds lower than 100 km/h

questions.prompt: When a driver is stopping behind another vehicle in traffic:
questions.explanation: Stop far enough back that you could steer around the vehicle ahead without reversing, for example if it stalls. A good guide is being able to see where its rear tires touch the road. Key words: "sufficient space".

choices.text: Keep back approximately 1 metre from the rear bumper of the vehicle ahead
Allow sufficient space to move into another lane without reversing
Remain a minimum of 10 metres from the vehicle ahead
Maintain sufficient space as determined by the 2-second rule

questions.prompt: When travelling in urban areas, drivers should scan the road approximately:
questions.explanation: In urban areas, look about 12 to 15 seconds ahead, roughly one city block, so you can spot hazards early. Key words: "scan the road".

questions.prompt: When driving in rural areas, how far ahead should you look?
questions.explanation: In rural areas, look at least 20 to 25 seconds ahead. In urban areas, look 12 to 15 seconds ahead. (Driver's Guide p. 89)

questions.prompt: How often should you check your rear-view mirrors while driving?
questions.explanation: Glance in your rear-view mirrors every 8 to 12 seconds, and whenever you expect to slow or stop. (Driver's Guide p. 89)

questions.prompt: Which of these is a variable hazard (one that changes during the day)?
questions.explanation: Variable hazards change, such as pedestrians, left-turning vehicles, icy roads, stale green lights, and emergency vehicles. Curves, hills, and intersections are fixed hazards. (Driver's Guide p. 89)

choices.text: School children walking near the road

questions.prompt: What is proactive driving?
questions.explanation: Proactive driving means anticipating possible hazards and acting to reduce or avoid danger before it happens. Never assume other drivers will drive carefully. (Driver's Guide p. 89)

choices.text: Driving at the speed limit at all times
Reacting quickly once a hazard appears
Anticipating hazards and acting to avoid danger before it happens

questions.prompt: What following distance is recommended for drivers of large vehicles such as motor homes?
questions.explanation: Drivers of large vehicles, such as motor homes, should keep a minimum four-second following distance. (Driver's Guide p. 90)

questions.prompt: When road or weather conditions are poor, your following distance should be:
questions.explanation: Under normal conditions, keep at least two seconds. When conditions are less than ideal, increase your following distance. (Driver's Guide pp. 81, 90)

choices.text: Less than 2 seconds, so you can keep up with traffic
The same as in good conditions

questions.prompt: How many demerit points are given for distracted driving offences such as texting or using a hand-held phone?
questions.explanation: The Traffic Safety Act sets a fine and three demerit points for distracted driving offences. (Driver's Guide p. 91)

questions.prompt: Which of these is a distracted driving offence under the Traffic Safety Act?
questions.explanation: Entering information into a GPS unit while driving is a distracted driving offence, along with texting, using hand-held phones, reading, and personal grooming. (Driver's Guide p. 91)

choices.text: Entering a destination into a GPS unit while driving

questions.prompt: You need to make a phone call while driving. What should you do?
questions.explanation: Stop in a safe and legal place before making or receiving a call, or sending or reading a text. (Driver's Guide p. 90)

choices.text: Use the phone only at red lights
Hold the phone below the window
Stop in a safe and legal place first
Make the call quickly while driving slowly

questions.prompt: A 17-year-old passenger in your vehicle is not wearing a seat belt. Who can be fined?
questions.explanation: Passengers 16 years of age and older who aren't properly secured can be fined themselves. The driver is responsible for passengers under 16. (Driver's Guide p. 91)

choices.text: No one, if the passenger is in the back seat

questions.prompt: Which children must be secured in a child safety seat?
questions.explanation: A child under six years of age who weighs no more than 18 kilograms (40 pounds) must be properly secured in a child safety seat. (Driver's Guide p. 91)

choices.text: Children under 6 who weigh 18 kg or less
Children who weigh less than 30 kg

questions.prompt: Forward-facing child safety seats are designed for children weighing:
questions.explanation: Forward-facing child safety seats are designed for children 10 to 18 kilograms (22 to 40 pounds). The tether strap must be used. (Driver's Guide p. 92)

questions.prompt: A child weighs more than 18 kilograms. What should they use before moving to the vehicle's seat belt alone?
questions.explanation: Children over 18 kilograms (40 pounds) should be secured in an approved booster seat before using only the vehicle's seat belt. (Driver's Guide p. 92)

choices.text: An adult seat belt worn under the arm

questions.prompt: What label must a child safety seat used in Canada have?
questions.explanation: All child safety seats used in Canada must have a label stating they meet Canada Motor Vehicle Safety Standard 213. (Driver's Guide p. 91)

choices.text: A label from the store where it was bought
A label stating it meets Canada Motor Vehicle Safety Standard 213

questions.prompt: You are feeling tired while driving on a long trip. What should you do?
questions.explanation: If you feel tired, stop for a rest and walk around your vehicle. Fatigue slows reactions and impairs judgement. (Driver's Guide p. 107)

choices.text: Open the window and keep driving
Turn up the heat to stay comfortable
Drive faster to finish the trip sooner

questions.prompt: When does impairment from alcohol or drugs begin?
questions.explanation: Impairment begins with the first drink or drug use. (Driver's Guide p. 108)

choices.text: With the first drink or drug use
Only above a blood alcohol level of 0.08

questions.prompt: A GDL driver is found to have any alcohol in their body while driving. Under the IRS ZERO: Novice program, the penalty includes:
questions.explanation: IRS ZERO: Novice brings an immediate 30-day licence suspension, a seven-day vehicle seizure, and a $200 fine plus a 20 per cent victim fine surcharge. (Driver's Guide p. 112)

choices.text: A 30-day licence suspension, a 7-day vehicle seizure, and a $200 fine

questions.prompt: The IRS: WARN program applies to drivers with a blood alcohol concentration of at least:
questions.explanation: IRS: WARN applies at 50 milligrams of alcohol in 100 millilitres of blood (0.05) or more. IRS: FAIL applies at 80 milligrams (0.08). (Driver's Guide p. 112)

questions.prompt: Which of these leads to an IRS: FAIL penalty?
questions.explanation: IRS: FAIL applies to a blood alcohol concentration of 80 mg or more, impairment by alcohol or drugs, or refusing without reasonable excuse to comply with a test demand. (Driver's Guide p. 113)

choices.text: A blood alcohol level of 0.03 for a fully licensed driver
Taking prescribed medication that has no side effects
Refusing a breath test demand without a reasonable excuse

questions.prompt: What happens to the vehicle when someone is caught driving while their licence is suspended?
questions.explanation: The vehicle is seized and impounded for 30 days, regardless of who the registered owner is. The owner pays towing and impound fees. (Driver's Guide p. 115)

choices.text: Nothing, if someone else owns it
It is impounded for 30 days, no matter who owns it

questions.prompt: A load extends 1.5 metres or more past the rear of your vehicle. What is required during daylight?
questions.explanation: During daylight, attach a red flag at least 30 centimetres square to the end of the load. At night, use a red light. (Driver's Guide p. 95)

choices.text: A yellow flag of any size
A red flag at least 30 cm square on the end of the load

questions.prompt: May passengers ride in the open box of a pickup truck?
questions.explanation: No. You must not allow anyone to ride on the outside of your vehicle, including the open box of a pickup truck. Both you and the rider can be charged. (Driver's Guide p. 95)

choices.text: No, it is illegal, and both the driver and rider can be charged

questions.prompt: In a residential area, during which hours must you not operate a vehicle in a way that disturbs residents?
questions.explanation: In a residential area, you must not operate a vehicle in a way that disturbs residents between 10 p.m. and 7 a.m. (Driver's Guide p. 95)

questions.prompt: Driving without due care and attention, or without reasonable consideration for others, is called:
questions.explanation: Driving without care and attention, or without reasonable consideration for others, is careless driving, which carries 6 demerit points. (Driver's Guide pp. 95, 109)
